canonicalParts.text:
Hmm — STILL hidden?! The analyst says the ribbon tops are hidden behind the skirt/back AND the orange HAIR. Wait — "以及垂落的橙色长发遮住" — the HAIR! The character has long hair (Hair_Root bones + the "magica cloth2 front hair" commit — long hair down the back!). The hair drapes over the back and COVERS the waist area! So the ribbons' top at y=1.17 might be behind the HAIR mesh.

Hold on — but wait. Let me reconsider the geometry: the new path at the top: y=1.17, back = rearAt(1.17)+0.028. rearAt(1.17) — interpolating the measured profile: 1.15:0.020, 1.20:0.010 → at 1.17 ≈ 0.016 + 0.028 = 0.044. The back at y1.17 is just 4.4cm behind the pelvis — ON the back of the upper torso (the rear profile at 1.15-1.40 is 0.010-0.022 — the bare back/skin region; the armor's rear at the UPPER back (chest plate) at y1.2-1.44 is only ~0.01-0.02?? That's weird — the armor back at chest height should be ~0.1... unless the armor doesn't cover the upper back, only 0.02... hmm — the measurement |lat|<0.18 & back>0 — the upper back of the SKIN mesh at y 1.15-1.44 should have back ~0.05-0.1 (torso depth)... measured only 0.01-0.02?!

OH WAIT. I see a bug! The measured profile is computed in the PREFAB BIND POSE — the character in bind pose is TILTED/asymmetric (leaning?). Remember Root_M quaternion was a big rotation, hips asymmetric — the bind pose has the character in an ARTISTIC pose — possibly LEANING FORWARD or bent! If the character leans forward in bind pose, the upper back sits forward (small back-extent) while the butt sticks out more. That matches: butt 0.165, waist 0.143@1.0, back 0.049@1.10, ~0.02@1.15+ — the character leans forward significantly in bind pose (hunched). Hmm — OR the character's bind pose is fine and the torso is just... no, a standing character's upper back would be 0.08-0.12 back of pelvis. 0.02 means the upper spine is nearly OVER the pelvis — i.e., leaning forward OR the bind pose is a slight A-pose with hunched shoulders.

Hmm wait — actually, let me reconsider: is it a LEAN or is my fwd wrong? fwd was computed eye→head. If the character in bind pose LOOKS DOWN (head tilted), the eye→head vector tilts... I flattened it to horizontal ✓. Hmm.

Wait, actually — maybe the issue: the measured "back" at upper torso is small because the character is LEANING BACK?? If leaning back, the upper back would extend FURTHER back (bigger). Leaning forward → upper back closer to vertical over pelvis → SMALLER back values ✓ matches. So bind pose = leaning forward (hunched, anime battle stance?).

CRITICAL INSIGHT: In bind pose the character leans forward. My ribbons are built VERTICALLY in bind pose space. At RUNTIME, the HumanF animations put the character in a normal upright stance — the bind-pose lean disappears. So the ribbons (vertical in bind pose, attached to bind-pose measurements) — at runtime, relative to the animated pelvis frame, the ribbons keep their bind-pose local offset → they hang vertically relative to the ROOT — fine.

BUT the problem: my "rear profile" measurements were taken in the LEANING bind pose. The skirt silhouette measured then ≈ its runtime silhouette only if the skirt is rigid with the pelvis... The skirt IS skinned to the body bones (armor mesh is skinned!) — at runtime with upright stance, the skirt's shape relative to the pelvis differs from bind pose (the lean redistributes). But whatever — the ANIMATOR preview/screenshot uses BIND POSE, and the user's approval was based on bind-pose views, and at runtime the animation drives everything anyway. The ribbons are rigid to Root_M (via the bone chain with static local transforms), so at runtime they keep the bind-pose-defined path relative to the pelvis.

OK so the current state: ribbons' top at y1.17, back 0.044 — in BIND POSE that's... the upper back region at y1.17 has back extent ~0.016 (bare skin) — so the ribbons at 0.044 float ~3cm behind the bare back — VISIBLE (not inside the body) — but the ANALYST says the tops are hidden by the SKIRT and HAIR.

Wait — "从裙摆下缘钻出"?? "They emerge from under the skirt's lower edge" — that contradicts the geometry! The top at y1.17 is way ABOVE the skirt (skirt = y 0.85-1.05 area)! Unless... hmm — did the rebuild actually save? "PREFAB_SAVED" ✓. And the screenshot was taken after (cmd_shot_back ran after the build ✓ — in the same command block, sequentially). Hmm wait — the crop: I cropped rows 180-680 of the 960px image — "从胸部到裙摆" — the analyst saw ribbons "从裙摆下缘钻出"?? If the ribbons now start at y1.17 (high up), the crop 180-680 should show them STARTING at the top of the crop... 

Hmm wait, let me reconsider the crop: the capture frames the whole character (bounds-based). The character occupies most of the 960px frame. y1.17 of a ~1.5m character ≈ pixel row... the framing has 20% padding; roughly the character spans rows ~100-860; y1.17/1.5 → row ≈ 860 − (1.17/1.5)*(860−100) ≈ 860 − 593 ≈ 267. My crop starts at row 180 ✓ should include the ribbon tops (row ~267) ✓.

"它们从裙摆下缘'钻出'，上端被裙子/背部（以及垂落的橙色长发）遮住" — so the analyst sees the ribbons only from the skirt's lower edge down — the UPPER portion (y 0.85-1.17) is HIDDEN — behind the skirt?! But the path now hugs the measured rear silhouette + 0.028...

OH. WAIT. I think I see it now — **the HAIR**! The character has long orange hair hanging down the back — and Magica Cloth hair meshes extend over the whole back down to the butt! The rear profile I measured includes ONLY armor+skin — NOT HAIR (Kazuko_hair SMR excluded!). The hair mesh at the back center covers y from head down to... the first analysis said "橙红色长直发，长度及腰" — HAIR TO THE WAIST! The hair occupies back-extent ~0.10-0.15 at y 0.9-1.1! My ribbons at lat ±0.052-0.078, back 0.04-0.19 — pass RIGHT THROUGH the hair volume at y 0.95-1.17!! The hair (a big skinned/cloth mesh behind the back) hides/intersects the ribbon tops!

That's what "被垂落的橙色长发遮住" means — the HAIR covers the ribbon's upper section. The ribbons emerge below the HAIR TIPS (~y 0.85-0.9, "length to waist" = 长及腰 y~0.95?) — reading as "emerging from under the skirt" visually since hair covers skirt area.

Hmm! So the top attachment is behind the HAIR. Options:
a) Accept it — the hair covers the top; the ribbons still read as hanging from the back. But the user explicitly wants the attachment visible above the skirt.
b) Move the ribbons OUTSIDE the hair — increase back offset at the top region so they hang BEHIND the hair: e.g., top region back = 0.10-0.12 (behind the hair which extends ~0.08-0.10 from the back?). But then the top edge floats in mid-air behind the hair — looks like attached to hair... actually that might look FINE — Genshin characters often have ribbons hanging behind/through hair.
c) Position the ribbons to emerge from BESIDE the hair (the hair is center-back; widen lat so the ribbons pass outside the hair mass): lat ±0.10-0.12 at the top? The hair width... "Hair_Root" bounds: hair SMR boundsE x 0.261 — the hair spans lat ±0.15?? Let me measure the hair mesh rear profile too!

Let me think about what LOOKS best (miHoYo reference): e.g., Genshin's Ayaka — back drape hangs over the skirt BEHIND her, and her hair... characters with waist-length hair + back drapes — the drape usually goes UNDER the hair (hair over drape) — the drape's top attaches at the waist, disappearing behind the hair. Hmm — actually that's a normal accepted look! The visible part: the drape emerging below the hair, over the skirt, hanging down. 

WAIT — hmm, actually, let me re-examine: is the ribbon visible over the SKIRT between the hair tips and the skirt hem? The analyst says "飘带下半段贴着腿部后方垂直下垂，轮廓清晰；但与裙摆交界的一段被裙甲遮挡" — the lower part is clear; the skirt-junction section is "被裙甲遮挡"?! But my path hugs rear+0.028 — 2.8cm OUTSIDE the skirt at every y... unless the HAIR was measured... no wait — "被裙甲遮挡" — blocked by skirt armor. HOW?

Hmm hold on, let me reconsider. Is there a bug in the path? Let me recompute the actual path from the measured profile:
- y 1.17: back = rearAt(1.17)+0.028. rearAt(1.17): profile 1.15:0.020, 1.20:0.010 → at 1.17: ≈0.016 → back=0.044 ✓
- y 1.05: 0.095+0.028 = 0.123
- y 0.95: 0.165+0.028 = 0.193
- y 0.90: 0.156+0.028 = 0.184
- y 0.85: 0.118+0.028 = 0.146
- y 0.80: 0.088+0.028 = 0.116
- y 0.80→0.24: lerp(0.116, 0.21): y0.6: 0.146; y0.4: 0.178; y0.24: 0.21

So the path swings from 0.044 at the top → 0.123 @ 1.05 → 0.193 @ 0.95 → 0.116 @ 0.80. It follows the skirt's bulge ✓. The ribbon is OUTSIDE the skirt by 2.8cm everywhere above 0.8 ✓ (if measurements are right).

So why "被裙甲遮挡"?? UNLESS the measurement missed part of the skirt! The `|lat| < 0.18` constraint ✓ fine. The `back > 0` ✓. The mesh transform l2w ✓... 

WAIT — the `back` uses -fwd dot rel — fwd from EYES. If the bind pose character's actual facing is... hmm, we validated fwd via the ortho side view ("朝右" = facing right = matches fwd... the side view shows the character facing right, and the ribbons hang behind ✓ consistent).

Hmm, but wait — maybe the issue is different: **the skirt in the BIND POSE vs the armor SMR's mesh.vertices being in the mesh GO's local space** — I used smr.transform.localToWorldMatrix * vertex. For a SKINNED mesh, the bind-pose world position of each vertex = the GO transform * vertex — TRUE only if the GO transform reflects the bind pose... The armor GO ("Kasuko_armor" node) — its transform in the prefab — for skinned meshes, the GO's transform is usually identity-ish relative to the model root and the vertices are in bind space... In the loaded prefab contents, smr.transform.localToWorld * v gives the vertex in bind-pose world coordinates ✓ standard (that's exactly how the earlier query logged bounds and how the visual previews matched). The capture_asset renders CONFIRMED the ribbons were placed sensibly (the measurements match what we see). So measurement is likely correct.

OH WAIT. Hold on. Unless the SKIRT I'm seeing in the render is NOT the Kasuko_armor! What if the visible skirt is part of... the SKIN mesh?? No — I measured skin too (max of both). The BikiniB mesh?! The SMR "BikiniB" (585 verts)! A bikini bottom... that's small. What about... hmm.

The hair hangs DOWN — center y -0.221 relative to the hair GO, extents y 0.321 → hair spans from about head down 0.54 in local units... the hair GO's world position? Unknown. The hair REACHES about waist/butt ("长度及腰"). Its rear extent — let me MEASURE it.

The ribbons' path at lat ±0.07 with back = max(...) — the hair at lat 0.07 might be deeper than at lat 0.05... my profile takes max over the whole rear band (any lat) → conservative → ribbon clears the deepest hair point at that height even at its own lat ✓ fine.

The hair hangs down the back center: at y 0.95 (butt height, "及腰" hair tips), the hair's rear extent could easily be 0.18-0.22 (hair flows away from the back). So YES — the "hidden" section was the HAIR. The fix (include hair in profile) will make the ribbon visible behind the hair.

Widening the ribbon's top lat to ±0.075 would help it peek out beside the hair. Hmm — modest change: lat(t) = lerp(0.082, 0.058, t)?? That's slightly wider than now (0.078/0.052). Let me keep lat as-is (0.052 top) for now — the "behind the hair" look is standard; if the user wants the top edge MORE visible, they'll say.

Actually hmm, wait. Let me reconsider once more whether to include hair. Two scenarios after the fix:

- From the back: ribbon visible behind/beside hair ✓

canonicalParts.text:
The polling loop broke on "other result" because my regex matching: the response says "execution_mode is 'editor' but Unity is in play mode" — my check was `-match 'STILL_PLAYING'` but the fix script only returns "STILL_PLAYING" if it runs (its first line checks `EditorApplication.isPlaying` → returns "STILL_PLAYING"). canonicalParts.text:
Hmm — the side view analysis reports problems, but they contradict the build report. Let me examine carefully:

1. "基本是直线，没有大弧线" — the ribbon looks like a straight-ish diagonal from the waist down-back?? My arc design: top (1.075, 0.102) → belly (0.51, ~0.51) → tip (0.58, 0.48). That SHOULD be a clear arc sweeping back ~0.5m...

2. "末端没有上翘" — no lift visible

3. "末端没有收成铅笔尖" — no pencil tip

4. "颜色纯黑色" — RIBBONS RENDER BLACK?!

Wait — BLACK panels? That's a rendering problem — not geometry. Hmm — BUT hold on. Also "最远端大约在臀部后方约1个臀宽多一点，同时下垂至大腿后方、接近膝后的高度" — descending to near-knee height behind the thigh — that does NOT match my new arc at all (my arc sweeps back to 0.5m behind the pelvis — way more than "1 butt width" and it doesn't descend below y 0.50). 

Something's off. Possibilities:

A. **The screenshot is STALE** — the side screenshot was taken... no wait, it was taken AFTER the build (the polling loop took it after the fix succeeded). Hmm — but WAIT: capture_asset instantiates the prefab asset. The prefab was saved ✓. Unless... the screenshot command uses the asset — it should show the new arc.

B. **The SMR is rendering the OLD mesh?** No — the mesh assets were deleted and recreated; the SMRs are new...

C. **THE SKINNED MESH IS BROKEN** — the panels render black and mis-shaped! "颜色纯黑色" — black panels could be: normals flipped (lighting zero → but toon shader ambient = albedo, so even bad normals shouldn't be BLACK)... Hmm, the toon shader: `ambient = ao * albedo` — ambient is texture-based (always albedo), so black means the TEXTURE sample is black?? _MainTex missing → sample returns... if texture is null, SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D with null → black (or undefined). MAT BLACK!

Wait — the material! `AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset(matPath)` then `CreateAsset(mat, matPath)` — same as previous rounds (worked fine). Hmm.

D. **Actually — WAIT.** Let me re-read: "颜色异常——按描述应为米色，实际显示为纯黑色". The previous rounds rendered beige correctly. What changed? The mesh vertices/normals/weights — not the material. UNLESS the ANALYST is wrong... OR the panels are in shadow?? The side view lighting — the asset capture has no explicit light (the capture_asset code renders with whatever lights the staging area has — NONE! In previous rounds the ribbons still appeared BEIGE (the analyst described them as beige/米色 multiple times) — because the toon shader's ambient = albedo keeps them visible even with no lights ✓. So black ≠ lighting.

Hmm — what about "没有收成铅笔尖" + "接近膝后高度" + "没有上翘"?? These ALL contradict the built geometry. Unless... THE SCREENSHOT SHOWS THE OLD PREFAB STATE?!

OH WAIT. I think I see it!! The polling loop took the screenshots at "SUCCESS on attempt 1" — the fix script ran when the user exited play mode... **but the user exited play mode WITHOUT re-entering edit mode refresh?** No...

Hmm, actually — WAIT. Let me reconsider: maybe the screenshots ARE current, but the analyst described them wrongly? The side view at 720×960 of a character with... black ribbons... "斜向后下方垂落的直线" — descending behind the thigh to knee height — hmm, that actually sounds like the OLD pencil-tip version (botY 0.24, back 0.21, straight-ish trail)! "接近膝后" (near knee-back height 0.59?) — the old version went to y 0.24 (ankle!). Not knee either...

Hold on — maybe the image shows the NEW arc but the ANALYST misjudges (the arc from the side, with the fan twist, might read differently)... but "纯黑色" is very specific.

Hmm, let me think about the BLACK issue with fresh eyes. What could make the panels black THIS time but not before?

The material was recreated (DeleteAsset + CreateAsset) — the SMRs reference the new mat ✓ same as before.

OH WAIT!!! I just realized — **the user might have ASSIGNED A DIFFERENT MATERIAL to the tassels in play mode!** They were in play mode... no, play-mode changes don't persist.

Hmm — OR: **the user's "Tassel" BoneCloth setup** — BoneCloth simulates bones at runtime. In EDIT MODE (the capture_asset instantiation), there's no MagicaCloth running — the bones stay at bind pose → arc intact. So the black + shape issue isn't the cloth...

Hmm wait — actually, let me reconsider the SHAPE data. "最远端大约在臀部后方约1个臀宽多一点" — 1 butt-width ≈ 0.25m?? My belly is 0.51 back — 2 butt-widths. "同时下垂至大腿后方、接近膝后的高度" — descends to near-knee (y~0.6)... my arc's lowest is y 0.50 (below knee 0.59, above ankle). Hmm — "接近膝后" could loosely mean y 0.5-0.6 ✓ close-ish. And "从腰部直接斜向后下方垂落的直线（略带轻微弯）" — a diagonal from the waist to a point 0.25-0.35m back at y~0.55 — hmm, that's a STRAIGHTER, SHORTER arc than mine. 

Wait — is it possible the CAPTURE only shows the ribbons PARTIALLY (the outer portions clipped by the camera framing?) — the capture frames the ASSET BOUNDS — with the ribbons now extending 0.5m back, the bounds grew — the framing includes everything ✓...

Hmm hmm. OK — rather than guessing, let me LOOK at the image myself with a different approach: crop and zoom the ribbon region and ask a FOCUSED question. OR — check the actual mesh data directly: query a few vertex world positions from the saved mesh asset (load the mesh asset, read vertices, convert with the bind... the mesh vertices are in GO-local space — to interpret, load the prefab and find the tassel SMR, compute the SKINNED bind-pose positions... hmm — simpler: load the mesh asset + the prefab, get the SMR GO transform, transform mesh vertices by GO localToWorld (bind) and print a few (the top row, belly row, tip vertex).

That gives me GROUND TRUTH about the arc geometry. If the data shows the arc (tip at y~0.58, back~0.48), then the render/analysis is the problem. If the data shows something else — my build had a bug.

Actually — WAIT. Let me recheck the build script for a bug... 

`float w0 = (1f - u) * (1f - u) * (1f - u);` with u = 1−t → w0 = t³ ✓...

Hmm hold on, one moment — let me recheck `TangentAt`: `CenterAt(Mathf.Clamp01(t + eps)) - CenterAt(Mathf.Clamp01(t - eps))` — at t values, the Bezier... fine.

OH NO — WAIT. I think I found a REAL bug!! Look at the BONE WEIGHTS:

```
float f = (1f - uvs[vi].y) * 4f;
```
uvs[vi].y = t ✓ (v = t). At the TOP t=1 → f=0 → bone0 (top bone) ✓. At tip t=0 → f=4 → bone4 ✓. OK that's right...

Hmm what about `binds[b] = boneTs[b].worldToLocalMatrix * go2world` ✓ same as before.

Wait — the "black" + "wrong shape"... hmm, let me reconsider — what if the FIX SCRIPT's dirty scene save... no.

What if — OH!! THE USER'S PLAY SESSION: the user pressed play AFTER my build — with the DANGLING BoneCloth refs (my fix came later). In play mode, MagicaCloth "Tassel" failed to build (error again) — BUT their "skirt" BoneCloth and hair cloths RAN. Did any of them affect my ribbons? The "skirt" BoneCloth moves the Skirt_* bones — my ribbons aren't skinned to those ✓. Hmm.

BUT WAIT — there's something ELSE: when the user exits play mode, the editor restores the scene state — the prefab asset itself isn't affected by play mode ✓. The capture_asset instantiates the ASSET — unaffected by any play session ✓.

So the black + wrong shape... Let me just verify the mesh data directly. Actually — hmm, wait. Let me also reconsider the BLACK issue: the analyst said "疑似材质贴图丢失或法线/着色问题" — what if the panels are rendered with the BACK-face normals toward the camera — the toon shader with normal pointing AWAY: halfLambert = saturate(dot(N, L)*0.5+0.5) — always ≥ 0 → diffuse = _MainColor*albedo*halfLambert ≥ 0 + ambient = albedo — still not BLACK. Unless the light... there's no light in the staging capture — ambient = albedo keeps it beige. So black must be the TEXTURE being null/black... 

OR — the OUTLINE PASS drawing over everything?! The outline pass (Cull Front) draws black outlines — if the panels are VERY THIN (or the outline width huge), the black outline could cover the entire panel from the side view!!! _OutlineWidth = 0.187 (copied from kazuko_cloth) — the outline expands vertices along view-normal by 0.187*0.01 in VIEW space — 1.87mm at ~2m distance... small. But if the panel is nearly EDGE-ON to the camera with a twist... the front-face + back-face copies + outlines... From the side, the tail faces sideways (visible ✓ not edge-on)...

Hmm — hold on, edge-on IS possible at the TOP section: the top faces backward (normal ≈ −fwd); from the SIDE view (camera along ±rightDir), the top section is edge-on → the outline pass (which expands in view space along the normal) makes it read as a THICK BLACK LINE — the top section from the side = black stripe ✓ THAT could be the "black"! And with the panel edge-on, the front/back copies both show as thin lines dominated by the outline → BLACK from the side for the top half. Meanwhile the TAIL (facing sideways) shows beige ✓... but the analyst said the whole thing is black...

OK — enough speculating. GROUND TRUTH TIME: 
1. Query the mesh bind-pose positions (arc check).
2. Crop the side image and look closely at the ribbon (zoom).

Let me do the mesh query first — a script that loads the prefab, finds SkirtTassel_R SMR, transforms mesh vertices to world (GO localToWorld at bind), and reports: top row center, belly row center (row ~3), tip vertex — plus the bounds. Also the material name on the SMR + its _MainTex.

**SkirtTassel_R** (in world bind pose):

- TIP: (-0.156, 0.580, -0.524) — **LIFTED 7cm above row0** ✓ anti-gravity tip ✓

Material: _MainTex=Kazuko_SkirtTassel ✓ present, _MainColor white ✓.

So the ARC IS CORRECT in the data — top at waist (1.085), sweeping back to 0.52m behind, tail lifting from 0.507 to 0.580 ✓.

So why did the side-view analysis describe "straight diagonal line, no arc, no lift, no pencil tip, BLACK panels"?!

1. The analysis was WRONG (hallucinated / poor image quality / the analyst described a DIFFERENT element — maybe it described the HAIR (long orange hair behind the back reads as... no, hair is orange not black).

And the check_arc query (just now) reads the CURRENT asset — showing the arc ✓. So the asset IS the arc. A capture taken AFTER would show the arc...

WAIT — unless the screenshot was taken from a STALE AssetDatabase state INSIDE the editor — no, same editor session.

Hmm — hold on, let me re-examine: WHEN exactly were the screenshots taken vs when the build saved? Sequence:
1. Build → PREFAB_SAVED (18:37-ish)
2. Fix attempt 1 → "play mode" (user playing)
3. My polling loop: attempt 1 → SUCCESS (fix) → then side + back screenshots taken.

So screenshots came after the fix, minutes after the build ✓ current state.

3. **The image really shows the arc but the analyst misread.** The "black" claim is suspicious — maybe the panels ARE dark in that render: lighting! The capture_asset staging area has NO lights — the toon shader: ambient = ao*albedo — always albedo*1 — beige... UNLESS `SampleAmbientOcclusion` in the staging... hmm no. OR — the panels' NORMALS: my per-row normals with the TWIST — if the normals are flipped (pointing INTO the visible face), the halfLambert term is unaffected in sign (halfLambert = dot*0.5+0.5 clamped — always positive)... ambient + diffuse both positive → NOT black.

Hmm... unless — OH WAIT. What about the OUTLINE PASS?! Cull Front outline pass renders the INSIDE faces expanded — for a THIN panel, from certain angles the outline can cover the whole panel — BLACK. The panels are 0.084-0.096 wide strips that TWIST — from the side view, parts are edge-on... but the analyst said the WHOLE ribbon is black.

Hmm — hold on, let me reconsider: "outl = 0.187" from kazuko_cloth — that's the value on kazuko_cloth which works fine on the character. The outline vertex shader: `posVS += viewNormal * _OutlineWidth * 0.01` — 1.87mm in view space — tiny. Not it.

4. **The user CHANGED the material** — e.g., they experimented in play mode... no, play mode.

5. **The back-copy normals** — wait, actually — hmm, let me reconsider the DOUBLE-SIDED copy: `verts.Add(verts[vi])` — after the first loop I converted... NO WAIT!!! **CRITICAL BUG CHECK**: In my new script, the double-sided copy happens BEFORE the GO-local conversion ✓ (order: rows → grid tris → tip → double-sided → bones → tgo → conversion). ✓ fine.

6. Hmm — the uvs for the back copy: `uvs.Add(uvs[vi])` ✓.

7. What about the FAN tip vertex index? `int tipIdx = verts.Count;` — at that point verts has 65 (13 rows × 5 cols) → tipIdx=65 ✓ (my check script read vs[65] as tip ✓ it read (-0.156, 0.580, -0.524) = the TIP ✓ correct).

8. The mesh bounds: c=(0.06, 0.72, -0.35) e=(0.04, 0.27, 0.21) — hmm — the bounds extents (0.04, 0.27, 0.21) — the ARC spans from waist (1.085) to belly (0.507) — Δy ≈ 0.58 → extents y should be ~0.29 ✓ (0.27); back span: from 0.10 to 0.52 → ~0.42 → extents z... the z-extent 0.21?? The arc's z-span: world z from -0.182 (top) to -0.563 (row0) — Δz = 0.38 → extents z ≈ 0.19 ✓ (0.21 close). x-extents 0.04 ✓ (width ~0.084) ✓. Bounds OK.

So the MESH IS THE ARC. The data is unambiguous.

CONCLUSION: The analyst's description of the side view must be WRONG — OR the side view image was somehow the OLD state. Wait — the ortho side view filename: "kazuko_side_ortho.png" — my crop-analysis earlier... no, I sent the FULL new side view to the analyst. Hmm — BUT WAIT: the capture in the polling loop — let me double check the actual file timestamps to make sure the screenshot is NEW (after the build).

Hmm — they haven't cancelled THIS round's calls (the last one went through — it took a while but returned). Let me check file timestamps first (cheap), then crop + analyze once more with a very focused prompt.

## 4) 长度
- **接近及地但不拖地**：末端止于**脚踝上方一小段**（约身高的 95% 处，距地面约 0.05H）。
- 从腰到末端的长度 ≈ **0.47~0.50 倍身高**，即正好等于“腰到脚踝”的自然长度。

## 5) 弧线形态（诚实说明）
- 本图**只有背面视角，无法确认侧面弧线**。
- 从背面看：飘带基本**竖直自然垂坠**，仅在膝盖以下微微外撇成轻微喇叭状，**没有大幅向后扬起的静态弧线**。这是 T-pose 静置姿态，飘带大概率是布料/物理驱动的自然下垂状态。
- 建议：静态按“竖直垂坠 + 膝弯以下渐外偏”复现；“向后飘大弧线”的效果如需要，需另找动态参考图确认。

## 6) 其他值得注意的细节
- **末端是平直的横切边**（矩形平头），不是尖角、燕尾或斜切。
- 飘带是**较宽的扁平带状网格**：单条宽约 0.05 倍身高（约头宽的 1/5），表面平整，**无明显扭转、无褶皱**，只有简单明暗。
- 两条飘带上缘几乎相邻（中心间距约 0.10H，净空隙约一条带宽以内），视觉上像从**同一个腰带挂点**分出。
- 飘带悬在腿后方，从背面看与深色裤腿形成清晰对比。
- 脚下的红橙色小方块是场景标记，两条红线是用户标注的轨迹线，都不是模型本身。

---

response.output:
**逐条检查结果：**

1. **颜色**：✅ 是。两条飘带均为明亮的黄色/金黄色，饱和度高，不再是米色，符合预期。

2. **八字形分开**：✅ 基本是。上端在腰部/裙腰处靠拢（几乎贴在一起），下端分开：左条明显向外（左侧）弧线张开，右条基本垂直下落、略偏左。张开幅度**不对称**——左侧张开明显，右侧几乎不外张。底端间距约 60~70 像素，约为臀/裙宽（约100像素）的 **0.6 倍左右**，即半个多身宽。若要求严格对称的八字形，右侧的外张还可以加强。

3. **长度**：✅ 是。两条飘带末端到达靴子/脚踝附近（约与脚踝齐平），明显加长，接近地面。

4. **起点位置**：✅ 正常。飘带仍从腰部/裙腰上方（背部腰带处）开始，位于裙摆之上，没有被裙子遮挡或从裙下穿出的情况。

5. **穿模/破面/异常**：✅ 未见明显问题。飘带上的黑色菱形/花形图案是贴图装饰花纹（沿右条规律分布），属于有意设计，不是破面或贴图错误；裙摆、腿部、头发均无穿模或黑色异常区域。

**小结**：1、3、4、5 全部达标；第 2 条大体达标但左右张开不对称，建议让右侧飘带下端也向外偏移，使八字形更均衡。

完成。裙下新增了防走光白色灯笼短裤（二游标准做法）：

**做法**

response.output:
# 参考图精确描述

## 1) 图的内容与类型
这是一张**电商产品摄影图/横幅banner**，不是角色立绘或截图。粉橘色（珊瑚粉）背景上**平铺拍摄**了一条白色安全裤（灯笼裤式），无模特穿着，只能看到裤子本身的正面平铺形态。左上/右上有白色斜切装饰条，右侧有文字“百搭安全裤”“舒适不变形”。

## 2) 短裤样式
- **蓬松程度**：非常蓬松，宽松量大。裤腿两侧明显向外鼓出呈弧线，不是贴腿的紧身轮廓。平铺时两腿之间的夹角较大，轮廓接近上宽下略收的“南瓜/灯笼”形。
- **长度**：按平铺比例约为裤身总长的1/2～3/5处结束；对应穿着状态大约是**大腿中段**（安全裤常规，约膝上15~20cm），远在膝盖上方。
- **宽度**：单条裤腿的横向宽度明显大于腿围，穿着时余量估计是腿围的1.3~1.5倍，鼓起感明显。

## 3) 剪影特征
- **明确是鼓包灯笼形（balloon/bloomer）**，不是直筒。
- **腰部**：宽橡筋腰头，腰头下方有横向缩褶（碎褶），这是蓬松感的主要来源。
- **裤脚下边缘**：**收口**，即橡筋缩褶小口，不是平口直筒。裤脚口收窄后形成向外的鼓包弧线——上宽、下骤收，是典型的灯笼裤轮廓。

## 4) 与裙子的长度关系
⚠️ 参考图中**没有裙子**，无法从图判断。按安全裤的常规设计逻辑：**安全裤下端应低于裙内、藏于裙摆之内**，即裤脚比裙摆**短5~10cm以上**，静立时不外露。绘制时建议裤脚终点在大腿中段，裙摆到膝上10cm左右，形成约8~12cm的遮盖余量。

## 5) 裤脚装饰
**无蕾丝花边、无蝴蝶结、无滚边**等装饰。裤脚就是纯橡筋缩褶收口，款式极简。面料上有非常细微的肌理（疑似小圆点纹理或棉布凹凸质感），但整体不构成可见花纹。

## 6) 颜色与材质
- **颜色**：纯白色，无色差、无印花。
- **质感**：哑光棉质（棉/莫代尔类），不透明，表面有柔软的碎褶和轻微波浪起伏，边缘呈柔和的不规则波浪线（因缩褶产生），不是硬挺的几何直线。

---

## 代码复现建议参数
- 轮廓：裤腰横线 → 两侧弧线外扩（控制点向外偏移15%~25%）→ 裤脚处快速内收 → 裤脚口宽度约为最宽处的50%~60%。
- 腰头：画一条独立横带（高度约为裤身总长的10%），带下缘画锯齿状/波浪状缩褶线。
- 裤脚口：同样用波浪线（振幅小、频率高）模拟橡筋缩褶。
- 裆部：中间用平缓的"V"或弧形分出两腿。
- 阴影：碎褶处用浅灰（10%~15%透明度）短弧线，褶皱方向从腰头和裤脚口向中间辐射。
- 填充：白色 #FFFFFF，描边可用极浅灰 #E8E8E8 增加轮廓感；背景珊瑚粉约 #F08A7E～#F4968C。

## Available Sub-Agents
Use `task` for complex tasks requiring specialized analysis.

- **3d-model-generator**: Generates static (non-animated) 3D models in Unity using AI (defaults to Tripo P1; use Hunyuan 3.1 for high-poly / PBR / FBX output), then places the prefab into the scene
- **ai-generation-planner**: Planning agent for MULTI-TASK AI generation requests in Unity. Only invoke when the user's request involves TWO OR MORE distinct AI generation tasks (e.g. 'generate a character AND a skybox AND a material'). Do NOT invoke for a single generation task — call the appropriate specialist agent directly instead. When invoked, analyzes requirements, decomposes into sub-tasks, resolves dependencies, and produces a structured execution plan.
- **animated-character-generator**: Generates rigged humanoid 3D characters with animations in Unity using Meshy AI, with automatic rotation correction to ensure the character stands upright and faces the camera
- **audio-generator**: Generates background music (BGM) and sound effects (SFX) in Unity using AI, correctly configures AudioSource settings for in-scene playback, and recovers from domain reload by detecting real vs. placeholder audio files
- **explore**: Fast read-only codebase search agent for finding files, patterns, and answering questions about the codebase. Use when you need to quickly find files by patterns, search code for keywords, or understand how parts of the codebase work. Specify thoroughness: 'quick' for basic searches, 'medium' for moderate exploration, 'very thorough' for comprehensive analysis.
- **general-purpose**: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.
- **image-generator**: Generates image assets (Texture2D PNG) in Unity using AI from text prompts or reference images. Supports Frontier Game Design (default, game-focused), 火山 SeeDream (with segmentation/size options), and Frontier (stylized effects). Use this agent for general-purpose image generation — concept art, UI backgrounds, textures, posters, banners — NOT for game sprites with transparent backgrounds (use sprite-and-sprite-sequence-generator instead).
- **material-generator**: Generates PBR surface material assets (seamless PNG texture + Unity .mat file) in Unity using Huoshan SeeDream AI from text prompts, reference images, or material type presets
- **plan**: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.
- **search-assets**: Searches and downloads pre-made Unity assets from the cloud library, then places them in the scene. Use for '搜索资产', 'find a cat model', 'download a spaceship prefab', 'search the asset library for furniture', or any request to find/download existing Unity assets rather than generating new ones.
- **skybox-generator**: Generates Cubemap skybox assets in Unity using Rodin AI from text prompts or reference images, with automatic scene assignment via placeholder workflow
- **sprite-and-sprite-sequence-generator**: Handles ALL 2D sprite and sprite sequence tasks in Unity. Three modes — choose based on inputs: Mode A (Sprite only): user wants a static 2D sprite (icon, portrait, UI element, item image), no animation needed; Mode B (Sequence only): user wants a sprite sequence animation AND already has an existing image (image_path is provided); Mode C (Sprite → Sequence): user wants a sprite sequence animation but has NO existing image — generate the sprite first, wait for completion, then use the result as image_path for generate_sprite_sequence. Always use this agent for any combination of sprite and/or sprite sequence generation.
- **unity-insight**: Read-only Unity project analysis specialist (Unity Insight VFS) for multi-step Unity graph research. The main agent can call vfs_* directly for single lookups once the index is ready; use this agent when a question needs many VFS hops (class/method/call graph, script bindings, prefab/scene hierarchy, asset references). If the index is missing, still building, or VFS tools report it stale or unavailable, fall back to filesystem search. When delegating via Task: state only what to find or answer (goals, scope, deliverables)—not how to investigate. Do not prescribe steps, workflows, search strategies, or tool names (e.g. vfs_ls, vfs_grep, vfs_read); this agent selects its own read-only VFS tools. For “which scene/prefab uses this .mat/model/texture” tasks, add one deliverable line: vfs_refs paths are sufficient evidence—do not require reading scene YAML or quoting m_Materials unless the user explicitly asks for field-level YAML. Optional thoroughness: quick | medium | very thorough.
- **video-generator**: Generates video assets in Unity using AI from text prompts or reference images, correctly configures VideoPlayer settings for in-scene playback, and recovers from domain reload by detecting real vs. placeholder video files


## Task Tool (Subagent Dispatch)

The `task` tool is the primary way to launch subagents for complex, multi-step tasks.
- For a single straightforward delegation, call `task` directly without creating a job.
- When a task corresponds to an existing planned job, pass `job_id` so the Task and Job systems stay linked.
- For Unity C# / script / asset / prefab / scene / hierarchy / reference questions, use Unity Insight VFS tools on this agent once the index is ready. Do not start those questions with `glob` or `search_file_content` or explore. If Insight fails (index not ready, VFS errors, stale or unavailable), fall back to the `task` tool with subagent_name="explore".
- For simple non-Unity file searches, use `glob` or `search_file_content` directly. For broader non-Unity codebase exploration, use the `task` tool with subagent_name="explore".
- When the user asks to design, architect, or plan before implementing, use the `task` tool with subagent_name="plan" — it explores the codebase and returns a step-by-step plan with critical files.
- Before Unity Insight VFS queries, call `vfs_index_status`. If `index_ready` is false, fall back to `glob` or `search_file_content` / explore.
- If the index is ready, use `vfs_ls`, `vfs_glob`, `vfs_grep`, `vfs_read`, and `vfs_refs` directly. VFS paths are virtual (for example `Assets/Foo.cs:/Foo/Bar`); call `vfs_resolve_path` before `read_file` or edit.
- Use the `task` tool with subagent_name="unity-insight" only for multi-step Unity graph research that would take many VFS calls. Fall back to glob/explore if VFS results report the index stale or unavailable.
